Age-adjusted 2021 suicide rates were highest among non-Hispanic American Indian or Alaska Native (AI/AN) persons (28.1 per 100,000) overall
Rates among persons aged 45–64 years decreased significantly overall (−12.4%) and among non-Hispanic Asian (Asian) (−15.9%)
Age-adjusted rates and 95% CIs were calculated using the direct method and the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Suicides were identified from the National Vital Statistics System multiple cause-of-death mortality files for 2018–2021.
Differences in rates from 2018 to 2021 were compared using z-tests when deaths were ≥100

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted rates and 95% CIs were calculated using the direct method and the 2000 U.S. standard population.
Differences in rates from 2018 to 2021 were compared using z-tests when deaths were ≥100;
When deaths were <100, differences in rates were considered significant if CIs based on a gamma distribution did not overlap.
Relative change was calculated using the following equation: (2021 rate – 2018 rate) / 2018 rate x 100
Rates are flagged as unreliable or suppressed when the rate is calculated with a numerator of <20
